facts.statement: Overosaurus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaurs named after the Cerro Overo locality where it was found.
facts.quote: Overosaurus (meaning "Overo lizard", after the Cerro Overo locality) is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaurs

facts.statement: Overosaurus was estimated to be approximately 10 meters long, making it relatively small compared to other Patagonian sauropods.
facts.quote: Overosaurus paradasorum was relatively small compared to other sauropods from Patagonia, like the saltasaurids and other aeolosaurines, estimated as approximately 10 m

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Overosaurus was recovered at the Cerro Overo locality in Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: The only known specimen of Overosaurus paradasorum was recovered at the Cerro Overo locality in Patagonia, Argentina

facts.statement: The Overosaurus specimen was collected in 2002 by researchers from the Museo Carmen Funes, the Museo Argentino Urquiza, and the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County.
facts.quote: The specimen was collected in 2002 by researchers from the Museo Carmen Funes, the Museo Argentino Urquiza, and the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County

facts.statement: The Overosaurus specimen is housed in the collection of the Museo Argentino Urquiza in Neuquén, Argentina.
facts.quote: This specimen is housed in the collection of the Museo Argentino Urquiza in Neuquén, Argentina

facts.statement: Carlos Parada and his family found the specimen and provided logistical support and fieldwork assistance to museum staff.
facts.quote: The specimen was found by Carlos Parada and family, who provided logistic support to museum staff as well as assistance during fieldwork

facts.statement: The Cerro Overo locality was originally thought to be in the Anacleto Formation but is now attributed to the Bajo de la Carpa Formation.
facts.quote: The Cerro Overo locality was originally reported as within the Anacleto Formation of the Neuquén Group, but is now attributed to the Bajo de la Carpa Formation

facts.statement: Overosaurus was described and named by Rodolfo A. Coria, Leonardo S. Filippi, Luis M. Chiappe, Rodolfo García, and Andrea B. Arcucci in 2013.
facts.quote: Overosaurus was described and named by Rodolfo A. Coria, Leonardo S. Filippi, Luis M. Chiappe, Rodolfo García and Andrea B. Arcucci in 2013

facts.statement: The sacrum of Overosaurus consists of six fused sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: Its sacrum consists of six fused sacral vertebrae

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Overosaurus within the Aeolosaurini as the sister taxon to a group containing Gondwanatitan faustoi, Pitekunsaurus macayai, Aeolosaurus rionegrinus, and Aeolosaurus maximus.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis of Lithostrotia placed Overosaurus within the Aeolosaurini, as the sister taxon of a monophyletic group formed by Gondwanatitan faustoi, Pitekunsaurus macayai, Aeolosaurus rionegrinus, and Aeolosaurus maximus

facts.statement: Overosaurus belongs to the family Saltasauridae.
Overosaurus belongs to the tribe Aeolosaurini.
Overosaurus paradasorum lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: Overosaurus paradasorum es la única especie conocida del género extinto Overosaurus, un dinosaurio saurópodo saltasáurido que vivió a finales del periodo Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 83 millones de años durante el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica

facts.statement: Overosaurus fossils were found in the Anacleto Formation of the Neuquén Group in Patagonia, southern Argentina.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en la Formación Anacleto parte del Grupo Neuquén, en la Patagonia al sur de Argentina

facts.statement: The genus name means 'Overo lizard' after the discovery site, while the species name honors Carlos Parada and his family for their generosity and cooperation during fieldwork.
facts.quote: el género significa reptil del Cerro Overo, en referencia al lugar en donde fue encontrado, y la especie es en honor a Carlos Parada y su familia, que siempre fueron generosos, útiles y cooperativos en los trabajos en el área del Rincón de los Sauces

facts.statement: Overosaurus lived between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Overosaurus lived approximately 86 to 84 million years ago in what is now Patagonia, southern Argentina.
rejected.quote: This species lived approximately 86 to 84 million years ago during the latter part of the Cretaceous Period in what is now Patagonia (in southern Argentina)
